system.name: Coach
system.one_liner: a system that exploits complementary temporal utilization patterns across VMs to oversubscribe all resources in cloud platforms

content.subject: how per-window predicted memory demand for two CoachVMs is turned into a shared server's guaranteed (PA) and oversubscribed (VA) memory backing

elements.role: predicted percentile (e.g. P95) utilization for a time window, setting the guaranteed portion

elements.name: PA-Demand
elements.role: guaranteed, physically-backed memory demand for one CVM/window

elements.name: VA-Demand
elements.role: oversubscribed, virtually-backed memory demand for one CVM/window (the gap between Pmax and PX)

elements.name: Sum of VM PA-Demand
elements.role: each CVM's PA-demand summed across CVMs

elements.name: Multiplexed VA-Demand
elements.role: the CVMs' VA-demand combined by taking the per-window maximum instead of summing, to save memory

elements.name: Server PA Backing
elements.role: the server's allocated guaranteed memory, sized to the summed PA-demand

elements.name: Server VA Backing
elements.role: the server's allocated oversubscribed memory, sized to the multiplexed VA-demand

elements.name: Total Memory Allocation
elements.role: the server's PA and VA backing added together

PA and VA backing are added to give the server's total memory allocation

content.key_idea: Because VMs' memory demands peak at different times, summing each VM's static guaranteed (PA) demand but multiplexing (taking the max, not the sum, of) their time-varying oversubscribed (VA) demand lets the server provision far less total memory than naive per-VM summation.

summary: Figure 16 works through Coach's memory-allocation mechanism for two 32GB CoachVMs sharing a 48GB server across three time windows (0-8hr, 8-16hr, 16-24hr). Panel (a) shows, per VM and per window, the predicted maximum memory utilization and a percentile (e.g. P95) prediction: the percentile sets the guaranteed, physically-backed (PA) demand, while the gap up to the maximum is the potential virtually-backed (VA) demand, with dashed red lines marking the per-window maximum thresholds the scheduler must respect. Panel (b) then maps these per-VM predictions onto shared server resources: each VM's PA-demand is simply summed across VMs to size the 'Server PA Backing,' but each VM's VA-demand is multiplexed, taking the maximum needed at each time window rather than summing, to size the smaller 'Server VA Backing.' Adding the two backing allocations gives the concrete example's total: 44GB (28GB PA-backed plus 16GB VA-backed) for two 32GB VMs, illustrating how multiplexing time-shifted demand saves memory versus naive per-VM summation.
summary_zh: 该图演示Coach的内存分配机制：(a)按时间窗预测两台32GB CoachVM的最大及P95利用率，P95部分为保证性PA需求，差值为VA需求；(b)将各VM的PA需求直接求和、VA需求按时间窗做多路复用取最大值，得到服务器PA+VA共44GB的分配，体现复用节省内存的原理。
